title: Blobstream retry log + format probes for checkpoint downloads
notes:
Context: intermittent failures when loading large checkpoints from GCS via blobstream. Seen primarily on nightly integration runs and some customer repros (dedicated nodes). Goal: reproduce reliably, collect error signatures, and enumerate short-term mitigations (client-side and server-side).

Quick summary of failures observed:
- Case A: partial tarstream then EOFError in loader: "EOF while reading chunk" (happens ~1/20 downloads, larger checkpoints > 60GB).
- Case B: checksum mismatch during per-shard verify (manifest reports SHA256 != computed). Fails fast.
- Case C: tar header parse error: "invalid tar header" after retrying with 3 parallel connections.

Commands / repro attempts (notes + outputs):
1) Baseline single-threaded copy (works more often):
   gsutil -m cp gs://checkpoints/prod-model/v3/checkpoint.tar /tmp/checkpoint.tar  # used as baseline
   Result: success on 9/10 runs, slow (~7-9m for 80GB).

2) Blobstream fetch via internal tool (blobstream client v0.17):
   ./blobstream fetch --manifest gs://checkpoints/prod-model/v3/manifest.json --out /tmp/cp_stream --parallel 4 --chunk-size 16MB
   Observed: Case A or C ~50% when parallel > 2. Logs show repeated socket resets, then EOF.

3) GCS range-get experiment (curl with range):
   curl -H "Range: bytes=0-10485759" -o part-0 https://storage.googleapis.com/checkpoints/...
   Verified content integrity for first several ranges. When a range returns shorter body (HTTP 206 but truncated), blobstream incorrectly continues.

4) Manifest vs on-disk checksum:
   python3 -c "import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open('shard-03','rb').read()).hexdigest())"
   Manifest: f2a9... ; computed: f2a8... (1-byte diff). Hypothesis: partial write or chunk overlap when parallel fetch reconstructs shard file.

Hypotheses / root causes to explore:
- Parallel range requests overlap by 1 byte on off-by-one in reassembly index; results in one shard being corrupt when boundary alignment crosses object chunk boundaries.
- GCS edge/proxy occasionally returns short responses for large range reads under concurrent load; client doesn't detect short body for 206 responses.
- Tar stream parsing fails if internal buffer splits header across underlying chunk boundary and code assumes header is contiguous. Race between streaming buffer refill + tar header parser.
- Checksum metadata might be for uncompressed data; if server-side compresses (gzip) for small ranges, recomputed hash mismatch. Unlikely but sanity check.

Quick patches tried locally:
- Forced serial fetch: blobstream --parallel 1 => drastically fewer errors (Case A/C drop to ~5%).
- Increase chunk-size to 64MB: fewer socket resets but larger memory pressure.
- Add verification after each assembled shard: if checksum mismatch, re-fetch that shard up to 3x with backoff. Reduced customer failures but increases latency.
- Change reassembly to assert no overlapping ranges: added sanity check to builder, discovered inconsistent index rounding in earlier version.

Logs / error snippets (copied raw):
- EOF:
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "loader.py", line 214, in load_checkpoint
      for member in tarfile.open(fileobj=stream):
    File "/usr/lib/python3.11/tarfile.py", line 1600, in next
      buf = self.fileobj.read(tarfile.BLOCKSIZE)
  EOFError: unexpected EOF while reading tar header

- Short 206 body detection (curl):
  > HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
  < Content-Length: 10485760
  < but received 10485758 bytes (2 bytes short)

- Checksum mismatch log: "shard-03: manifest sha256=f2a9... computed sha256=f2a8..."

Instrumentation ideas to add (server + client):
- Client: always validate Content-Length vs bytes received for 206 responses; treat short reads as failure and retry ranges.
- Client: include explicit per-range sequence numbers and byte-offset checks when reassembling to detect overlaps/holes before writing final shard.
- Server/infra: check GCS logs for short responses from edge nodes (ask infra: RW-ops to surface proxy errors for bucket).
- Runtime: make tar parser more tolerant by supporting buffered header reassembly (already local patch).

Small experiments I plan next (order):
1) Run synthetic generator: create 100GB tar of many small files, upload to staging bucket, run blobstream with parallel=4 and check failure rate. Purpose: reproduce on-demand in isolated environment.
2) Add strict range-length assertion in blobstream and run 200 downloads in parallel on staging to see if short reads spike.
3) Replace HTTP client lib with lower-level requests that exposes raw socket errors to see if underlying library swallowed a reset.
4) If repro stable, write small integration test that fuzzes boundary conditions (1B-32MB chunk size range) and run on CI with network emulation.

Temporary mitigations for release branch:
- Default blobstream parallel -> 1 for checkpoints > 40GB (config flag: CHECKPOINT_DEFAULT_PARALLEL).
- Add per-shard verify + aggressive retry (3 attempts) in loader.
- Roll out quick metric: checkpoint_download_failures / successful_download_duration to SLO dashboard.

Notes for handoff to infra/SRE:
- Please check GCS bucket metrics for 2026-02-14..2026-02-21 for objectReads, 5xx rates, and any proxy truncation logs. Mention JIRA-RW-2026.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How often is manifest generated by upload pipeline vs computed at upload time? Could manifest be stale? (ask build infra).
- Are we compressing at upload time (gzip) for some objects? Confirm Content-Encoding on objects.
- Should we add server-side signed URLs expiry longer for large multi-part clients? Race between re-fetch and expiry could cause partial reads.

If anyone wants to reproduce quickly: check out branch kai/checkpoint-robustness, run: 
  ./dev/integration/run_checkpoint_repro.sh --bucket gs://redwood-staging/checkpoints-sim --parallel 4 --runs 50 --chunk-size 16MB

Next steps (short):
- Implement read-length assert + retry in blobstream (WIP PR linked above).
- Run synthetic stress overnight and collect artifacts (logs + failing shard hex diffs).
- Sync with Maya/Devin on Monday to decide conservative default for prod.

Personal log: spent ~6h experimenting; serial fetch reduces failures but is not acceptable perf-wise for customer SLAs. Need to find minimal change that eliminates overlap/truncation without doubling latency.
